subject: Clarify: Hour-pool vs. Rate-card for POC extension
messages:
From: Emma Ruiz <emma@acclaro.ai>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acclaro.ai
Date: 2027-05-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC extension pricing question — hour pool vs rate-card

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited and we'd like to extend the 30-day POC by another 4 weeks while we validate throughput. Procurement asked me to clarify two things before we sign the addendum:

1) We saw two different pricing approaches in the proposal attachment: a per-token rate card and an hourly "burst" pool. Can you confirm how they coexist? Are we billed on tokens until we hit a burst event, or switching models?

2) If we use the hourly pool for heavier testing, what caps / surges apply? Procurement needs a hard cost ceiling (or predictable credit mechanism) so we can get internal approval.

Attaching our annotated SOW and a short list of procurement questions. Can you also confirm any minimum monthly commitment if we add the 4-week extension?

Appreciate quick clarity — procurement wants to review by Friday.

Thanks,
Emma Ruiz
Head of AI Ops, Acclaro Labs
Emma@acclaro.ai

Attachments: POC_SOW_v2.pdf (annotated), acclaro-questions-20270518.docx

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Emma Ruiz <emma@acclaro.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-19T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC extension pricing question — hour pool vs rate-card

Hi Emma — thanks for sending the notes and the SOW. Quick answers up front, then a short proposed hybrid that aligns with what procurement asked for.

Short answers:
- We do not force a model switch mid-request. The platform supports a baseline per-token billing (rate-card) for normal traffic, plus an optional hourly "burst pool" that you can enable for stress testing or load-heavy batches.
- Hourly pool = capacity units for a bounded window (hours). Usage from the pool is billed hourly at the pool rate; anything outside the pool reverts to per-token pricing.
- For cost predictability you can set a hard cap on pool spend (bill stops at cap) or an overage-to-credits flow (we bill up to cap and refund credits if usage falls below forecast).

Proposed hybrid for Acclaro Labs (summary):
- Baseline: per-token rate-card (no commitment change) for regular API traffic.
- Extension burst pool: a 160-hour pool (4 weeks of controlled burst windows) priced at the hourly pool rate in pricing_grid_acclaro.xlsx.
- Safety cap: hard cap at $18k for the pool. If you hit the cap we pause further pool consumption and fall back to token-rate (no surprise invoices).
- Surge protection: first 10% over expected baseline is free (absorbed by us once during the POC), subsequent burst usage pulls from the pool until cap.
- Discount: 10% off the listed hourly pool rate as a courtesy for POC extension conversion intent.

I'll attach the updated pricing grid and mark the pool rows. If procurement wants a formal addendum I can draft it today and loop legal.

Next step: If that approach sounds OK, can you confirm whether procurement prefers a hard cap (pause) or a soft cap (automatic credit reconciliation)? Once you confirm we can lock the addendum and send a DocuSign.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachments: pricing_grid_acclaro.xlsx

From: Emma Ruiz <emma@acclaro.ai>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acclaro.ai
Date: 2027-05-19T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC extension pricing question — hour pool vs rate-card

Grace — thanks, that clarifies a lot. Procurement is leaning to a hard cap (pause at cap) to avoid any month-end surprises. A couple of follow-ups:

- Can you confirm the effective 10% courtesy discount applies only to the pool hours for the extension window and not retroactive to prior usage?
- What SLA adjustments (if any) apply when the pool is active? We need to know whether burst traffic changes our latency SLO or support priority.

If you can confirm both, procurement will be comfortable signing the addendum.

Best,
Emma

Subject: Re: POC extension pricing question — hour pool vs rate-card

Looping in finance/ops here. Two quick confirmations from our side before we finalize:

1) Discount scope: the 10% courtesy discount is limited to the extension burst pool only and is not applied retroactively. That keeps billing reconciliation straightforward.

2) SLA: Enabling the pool does not change the standard POC support SLA. We guarantee the same priority support; however, if you request a dedicated on-call or higher SLA for the burst windows we can add that as a short-term support retainer (charged separately).

Also flagged: finance can accept a hard cap/pause model but asks for a $1k refundable security placeholder (refundable within 14 days after the pool window if usage < cap) — this protects us from unexpectedly high short-notice bursts. Happy to waive for deal conversion, but we wanted to surface it.

If that all looks good Emma, Grace can create the addendum and send the DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Head of Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
